title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Handler Exception Close Architecture
purpose: Define the accepted WebSocket tunnel server policy for unexpected application handler exceptions after the RFC 9220 response has been sent.
design_summary: After a WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnel is accepted with response headers, `Http3Server` catches unexpected non-cancellation, non-QUIC application handler exceptions, emits the server error diagnostic, writes a WebSocket close frame with status code 1011 and reason `internal error`, completes the writable side of the tunnel stream, and returns without escalating the exception to the connection loop.
data_and_state_considerations: The mapping is request-stream scoped and does not add scheduler or connection state. Application handlers that choose their own close codes still use `Http3WebSocketTunnelContext.CloseAsync` directly.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Cancellation and QUIC transport exceptions remain delegated to the existing expected-exception paths.
The close write is best effort because the peer might already have closed the accepted tunnel.
The policy is a generic 1011 fallback and does not infer application-specific close codes.
risks: A generic 1011 close could hide application detail from clients, so the server also emits the exception through existing diagnostics.
External peer behavior still needs live interoperability proof before promoting beyond local loopback evidence.
